reasons.specificity: The table and prose correctly identify the distinct argumentative architectures of each text—myth-cycle versus unbounded-markets framing, Simmel/Marx/Schumpeter synthesis versus Luhmann/Hayek/Economic Theology—and tracks how the same propositions (money as absolute means, creative labour, dynamic transcendence) migrate between them; it does not collapse into generic 'capitalism and religion' themes.
reasons.anchoring: Most key claims are paired with verbatim passages that genuinely support the interpretation: 'Present-day market radicalism tends to paralyse the working of the myth cycle' versus 'From within itself, the dynamic of these promises cannot be stopped'; 'weaning off the drug of absolute wealth' versus 'sobriety and realism'; and so on. A few cells (e.g. F7 on 'imaginations' replacing the myth cycle) are plausible inferences rather than anchored contrasts, since the 2022 text's single Beckert citation does not itself say it is replacing the earlier cycle theory.
reasons.non_obviousness: The analysis surfaces a genuine tension—earlier local paralysis versus later systemic unstoppability—and distinguishes two different causal chains supporting superficially similar growth claims. It also notes that the 2022 text's explicit continuity declaration concerns Marx, not Deutschmann's own 2001 piece, which is a precise and non-obvious observation about the direction of self-citation.
reasons.coherence: The table rows and prose generally align, and the finding-ledger entries match the paired anchors. However, the scope-assessment section introduces a dense administrative apparatus (inconclusive/unchecked on every dimension) that creates noise without adding comparative insight, and some rows in the table label absence of explicit cross-reference as a 'finding' while the body simultaneously treats implicit thematic continuity as substantive—a mild internal tension.
reasons.usefulness: A reader moving between the two texts will find the position map and the table practically helpful: they can see at a glance which propositions persist, which change in force, and which evidential frameworks replace earlier ones. The honest 'no explicit cross-reference found' result is clearly stated and useful for anyone uncertain whether the 2022 essay is self-consciously building on the 2001 article.
reasons.hallucination_risk: No fabricated citations or invented positions are detectable; every major claim is tied to a locatable passage. The one area of risk is the characterization of F7—that 'imaginations' (Beckert 2016) displaces the myth-cycle theory—since the 2022 text simply does not discuss its relationship to the earlier cycle framework; labelling this a 'displacement' goes slightly beyond what the text itself establishes, though the inference is defensible.

score.one_line: A well-anchored, non-obvious comparison that correctly identifies parallel propositions and real shifts in force and causal emphasis across the two texts, with only minor overreach in characterising the absence of the myth-cycle as an explicit displacement.
